content.comment_body: Hello, I have a static IP address and want to know if it's possible to connect to the [product_name] web server and control it remotely via the Internet. If yes, where can I find a detailed tutorial?

Greetings [user_name], Yes, you can remotely control [product_name] over the Internet using its web server. With a static IP, you should forward port 8080 on your router. There are several relevant video guides on YouTube. Check the attachment for a sample port forwarding setup – your router interface may vary, but the general configuration is similar. Also refer to this video: [url]. If you have further questions, feel free to ask.
Port forwarding alone exposes your home network to potential cyberattacks. For remote access, consider using services like DynDNS or a VPN for improved security.
Hello [user_name], That's correct—security is crucial. While port forwarding is suitable for testing, more secure measures should be used for long-term remote access.

For a long time, I thought having a static IP was the solution, until I tried it and immediately saw port scanning attacks in the router logs. It's alarming to see random login attempts every few seconds! To protect our devices, we host a VPN that remote sites connect to with authentication, offering secure communication as if on the same network. If you're not experienced with networking or TCP/IP, consider hiring a professional, or ask your ISP for assistance. For example: Static IP is not essential at the [product_name] site. 1) Get a hosted VPN or create your own; some routers like certain models are well-known and highly configurable for this. Use IPSec or the highest security available. 2) Configure your router/device's VPN to connect to the VPN host. Devices like those mentioned can be set up behind the main router; make sure to configure VPN login, IPs, gateways, and ports. Static IP isn't necessary—even for mobile connections with NAT. 3) Set up user accounts, routes, and ports in the VPN so they target your device. Multiple sites and devices can have unique IP ranges and routes. 4) Enable VPN access on your PCs or phones. With this approach, you gain full access to the [product_name] for programming and web page viewing. Another option is certain GSM modules, which operate only via mobile networks and need unrestricted APNs. Configuration is available for only one [product_name] per unit and emails are sent over mobile data. Full setup information is available in the respective [document] section. Let me know if you need more details.

Could someone provide detailed instructions for port forwarding the [product_name] web server? I want to test this capability regardless of security concerns. Specifically, what settings do I need to change in [product_name] programming software and my modem/router for port forwarding? The modem/router configuration page is attached.

Hello, These steps might help: 1- How do you activate and access the web server on [product_name] [version_no]? 2- To set up port forwarding in your router, set 'Remote side' to External Port 8080 and Internal Port 8080, directing it to the '[product_name] IP address.' For local PC access, use: http://[public IP address]:8080 or http://[domain]:8080 (with services like Dynu or dyn.com). 3- For a secure setup, establish a VPN connection between your PC and [product_name] [version_no].

While basic port forwarding is possible, several users highlighted the significant security risks, strongly advocating for secure alternatives such as VPNs instead of exposing ports. The discussion included requests for comprehensive, step-by-step guides on both basic and secure remote access, with multiple users emphasizing the need for safety and professional assistance.
